onboarding.welcomeIntro: SSH terminal, remote file management, and server monitoring in one window. Connect to a host and get a terminal on top, an editor for remote files in the middle, the file list below, and live CPU / memory / network graphs on the side.
onboarding.featureTerminal: Tabbed SSH terminal with split panes, search, command history, and snippets
onboarding.featureSftp: SFTP file manager: double-click to open/edit, drag to upload, batch transfer queue
onboarding.featureMonitor: Live CPU / memory / network / disk graphs and top processes
onboarding.featureManage: Grouped connection tree, port forwarding, encrypted credential vault, import/export
onboarding.updatedFromTo: Updated from v{{from}} to v{{to}}. Changes in this release:
onboarding.noNotes: This is a maintenance release with no user-facing changes.

sftp.conflictTitle: {{count}} item(s) already exist on the server
sftp.conflictDesc: These remote files would be affected by this upload. Pick one action for **this batch** — your default setting is not changed.
sftp.conflictOverwriteHint: “Overwrite all”: same-named files are replaced; folders are merged, other files already on the server are not deleted.
sftp.conflictSkipHint: “Skip all”: skips the top-level items listed above — an existing folder is skipped whole.
sftp.conflictRenameHint: “Rename all”: saves as “name (2).ext” on the server and leaves the originals untouched.
sftp.deleteIrreversible: This cannot be undone; directories are removed recursively.
sftp.fastDeleteWarning: This runs a shell command directly on the server. Deletion is immediate and permanent — no trash, no undo, no progress.

sftp.fastDeletePartial: Fast delete incomplete — {{count}} item(s) still present

sftp.fastDeleteUnknown: Could not confirm the result — refresh and verify

sftp.dropNoSession: Session is not ready yet — cannot upload

editor.emptyHint: Right-click a file in the SFTP list of the main window and choose “View in built-in editor”
editor.readOnlyHint: This file cannot be edited right now: still loading, or the read failed
editor.readOnlyLossless: Editing is disabled because the bytes do not decode cleanly with the current charset: they contain sequences that are invalid in it, so some characters shown here have already been replaced — saving would destroy those bytes for good. Pick another charset on the right, confirm the content looks right, then edit.
editor.charsetHint: Re-decode with this charset. If it looks like mojibake, pick another — switching only re-reads, the remote file is never written
editor.dirtyHint: Changes have not been written back yet. Ctrl+S to save
editor.savedWithWarning: Saved, but one thing did not work out: {{warning}}
editor.gateStuck: Save is stuck: a gate you already confirmed blocked the write again. Please reopen this file and try again
editor.conflictTitle: The remote file changed while you were editing
editor.conflictDesc: Saving now would overwrite someone else’s changes for good. Consider cancelling, hitting “Re-read from the server” to see what changed, then deciding.
editor.nonAtomicTitle: This server does not support atomic replacement
editor.nonAtomicDesc: A normal save writes a temp file and swaps it in with one step, so the remote file is complete the whole time. This server lacks the posix-rename extension, so the only option is “rename to backup → rename into place” — and between those two steps there is a very short window where the target does not exist. If a service is reading this file (nginx could reload at any moment), it may see an empty file during that window.
editor.shrinkTitle: The content is far shorter than what is on the server
editor.shrinkDesc: This looks like a mistake (select-all followed by an accidental keystroke, say). If you really do want the file cut down this far, go ahead.
editor.shrinkNumbers: The server has {{remote}} bytes; {{local}} bytes would be written
editor.shrinkOk: Yes, it should be this short
editor.discardDesc: This file has changes that have not been written back. Continuing throws them away for good.
editor.bomHint: The file starts with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF)
editor.losslessHint: The bytes do not decode cleanly with the current charset: they contain sequences that are invalid in it, so some characters shown here have already been replaced. Try another charset.
editor.mixedEolHint: This file mixes LF and CRLF. The editor shows everything as LF, so line numbers and content are correct; but **saving normalises line endings across the whole file** (to whichever one the status bar shows), so a save can never be byte-identical to the original.
editor.tooManyOpen: You can’t open more than {{max}} files at once — close some first
editor.notLoadedYet: The file hasn’t finished loading; try saving again in a moment
editor.sessionDead: The session for “{{origin}}” is disconnected: saving and reloading are unavailable for now; the content can still be edited and copied. Resumes automatically after the session reconnects
editor.closeWindowDirtyDesc: Closing the editor window will discard these changes. This cannot be undone.

Write the command to send — multiple lines are fine.
Ctrl+Enter sends.

For example:

tail -n 50 /var/log/nginx/error.log
commandEditor.autoEnterHint: Appends a newline, i.e. actually runs it. With this off the text just sits on the command line until you press Enter yourself
commandEditor.expandVarsHint: Before sending, replace these placeholders per target session:

conn.name: Name
conn.passwordSavedHint: Encrypted password saved; leave empty to keep it
conn.passwordEmptyHint: Leave empty to be asked on connect
conn.privateKeyRequired: Please choose a private key file
conn.flagHint: Pick a flag for where the server physically is, or 'LAN'. Left empty, private addresses (10./172.16/192.168…) show a LAN marker automatically.
conn.startupCommandPlaceholder: Command to run automatically after connect
conn.legacyAlgorithmsTip: Append ssh-rsa, dh-group14-sha1, aes128-cbc etc. for old switches/bastions
conn.monitorEnabledTip: Open the server monitor on connect. Holds one exec channel open — turn it off on constrained servers
conn.rdpDesc: On connect, a .rdp file is generated and opened with the system remote desktop client (mstsc on Windows). The password is handled by the system credential prompt — this app neither stores nor fills the RDP password. Leave the username blank to let the system ask.
conn.rdpLaunched: Opened in the system remote desktop
conn.proxyFollowVia: Follows the global default: {{name}} ({{addr}}). Change the default in Settings to switch all at once.
conn.proxyFollowDirect: Follows the global default: currently direct. Set a default proxy in Settings → Proxies & keys.
conn.proxyDirectHint: This connection forces a direct connection, ignoring the global default proxy.
conn.privateKeyPickHint: Save a key once and reuse it across machines (path and passphrase live on that record)
conn.proxyHint: Dial the target server through a local or remote proxy (e.g. Clash/v2ray mixed port 127.0.0.1:7890)
conn.proxyAuthOptional: Leave empty if the proxy needs no auth
conn.notePlaceholder: A short description for this machine, shown in the connection list

savedRef.desc: Set these up once, then pick them from a dropdown when adding a machine. Passwords and passphrases are still encrypted by the system keychain; the UI never sees the plaintext.
savedRef.defaultProxyHint: New connections use this proxy by default (as do connections set to 'Follow global'). Changing it takes effect live on all follow-global connections; connections set to direct or a specific proxy are unaffected.
savedRef.name: Name
savedRef.keyPathHint: Only the path is stored — the key material never enters this app or its export files
savedRef.keyPassHint: Leave empty if the key has no passphrase
savedRef.blockedTitle: “{{name}}” is still in use — nothing was deleted
savedRef.blockedDesc: These connections still reference it. Change them in the connection editor first, then come back:

update.upToDate: You are on the latest version
update.availableTag: v{{version}} found — downloading in the background
update.portable: The portable build cannot update itself — download the new version from Releases
update.note: New versions download in the background (only the changed parts). **Installing is always your call** — it requires quitting the app, so it never restarts on its own.
update.confirmBody: Installing quits the app. These will be disconnected: {{sessions}} session(s), {{transfers}} running transfer(s), {{forwards}} port forward(s).
update.confirmTail: Transfers are cancelled (partial data stays in .part and can resume later). The app quits and reopens once installed.

settings.exportDesc: Export connections, groups, snippets, forwarding rules, trusted hosts and UI settings to a JSON file. Uninstalling wipes local data — export first.
settings.exportIncludeSecrets: Include saved passwords (requires an export passphrase)
settings.exportPassphrasePlaceholder: Export passphrase, at least 8 chars; lose it and passwords are gone
settings.importDesc: Restore connections, snippets, forwarding rules and trusted hosts from an exported JSON file.
settings.importIncludeRefs: (plus {{proxies}} saved proxies and {{keys}} saved private keys)
settings.importIncludeSettings: UI and terminal settings (changes this machine right away)
settings.importPassphrasePlaceholder: The file carries encrypted passwords; the passphrase unlocks them
settings.importNoSecrets: This file holds no passwords — imported connections will ask for one on first connect.
settings.importConflictLabel: When the same item already exists
settings.importConflictSkipHint: Keep what is on this machine, import only what is missing.
settings.importConflictOverwriteHint: Replace the local item with the one from the file; local edits are lost.
settings.importConflictDuplicateHint: Always create new items with an "(imported)" suffix; local data is untouched.
settings.importInvalidWarn: {{count}} entries are incomplete and will be skipped
settings.importConflictWarn: {{count}} connections already exist here — handled by the policy below
settings.importResultSummary: Imported {{profiles}} connections, {{snippets}} snippets, {{forwards}} forwarding rules, {{knownHosts}} trusted hosts and restored {{secrets}} passwords.
settings.fsImportDesc: Reads a FinalShell data directory (it should contain a `conn` subdirectory) and brings over connections and groups. ⚠️ Passwords do not come across: FinalShell encrypts them with a key built into its own client, and this project does not guess that key — enter the password once on first connect and tick “remember”, and it will be encrypted by this machine’s key store.
settings.fsImportSkipped: Will skip: {{invalid}} structurally incomplete, {{notSsh}} non-SSH connection(s).
settings.fsImportConflict: When this machine already has the same target (host + port + user)
settings.confirmOnCloseTabHint: Only asks while the session is still connected
settings.autoCheckUpdateHint: Checks after launch and every 6 hours, downloading new versions in the background (changed parts only). Installing is always your call — it disconnects every session. You can still check manually under About.
settings.disableGpuHint: Enable if old GPU drivers cause a black screen; needs a restart
settings.restartRequired: This takes effect after restarting the app
settings.maskHostInListHint: Show only partial IP/hostname (e.g. 156.•.•.50) in the connection tree — enough to tell machines apart and safe for screenshots. The full address is still used for connecting, copy command, and search.
settings.webglHint: Falls back to the DOM renderer when off — safer, slightly slower
settings.saveCommandHistoryHint: Remembers the commands you run in the terminal; Ctrl+Shift+H brings them back. The history stays in the local database and is never included in exported app data. Turning this off only stops new entries — use “Clear list” in the overlay to delete what is already there.
settings.downloadDirHint: Leave empty to be asked each time
settings.conflictPolicy: When an upload name already exists
settings.conflictPolicyHint: With “Ask each time”, one batch asks once for all clashes — never one dialog per file.
settings.doubleClickActionHint: The context menu’s “Open” always edits; this only covers double-click
settings.followTerminalCdHint: After running cd in the terminal, the file panel jumps to that directory. Best-effort: `cd -` and paths with variables are not followed; if the directory can't be read, the panel stays put without raising an error.
settings.autoOpenOnConnectHint: Expands the SFTP split pane for new sessions. Whether the monitor opens is set per connection
settings.packedTransferHint: When downloading a whole directory, pack it into a single tar on the server, transfer that one file, then extract locally — orders of magnitude faster for thousands of small files (it removes the per-file round trips). This is advisory: too few files, no tar/mktemp on the server, not enough space, or an incompatible conflict policy all fall back to per-file transfer with the reason shown on that task. Downloads only for now.
settings.fastDelete: Offer "Fast delete" in the context menu
settings.fastDeleteHint: Removes a whole directory tree with rm -rf on the server — far faster than deleting entries one by one, but immediate, permanent and without progress. Directories only, and paths shallower than two segments (e.g. /etc) are rejected.
settings.vaultAvailableDesc: Passwords are encrypted by the OS keystore (DPAPI on Windows, bound to the current user).
settings.vaultUnavailableDesc: The OS keystore is unavailable, so passwords will not be saved — you will be asked on every connect.
settings.securityNotes: Stored passwords are never sent back to the UI layer; password and passphrase fields are redacted in logs. An existing vault cannot be decrypted after reinstalling the OS or moving machines — migrate via encrypted export.
settings.knownHostsDesc: Host key fingerprints you confirmed on first connect. Revoke one here if the server was legitimately reinstalled (fingerprint changed) or you trusted it by mistake — the next connection will ask for confirmation again.
settings.knownHostsRevokeDesc: This only withdraws the trust decision — connection profiles are untouched; the next connection to this host will re-confirm the fingerprint.
settings.exportEncryptAll: Encrypt the entire file (hosts and usernames too, requires an export passphrase)
settings.exportEncryptAllHint: The exported file contains no plaintext. Note: after at-rest encryption is enabled you cannot migrate by copying the .db across machines — use encrypted export/import instead.
settings.importEncryptedNote: This file is fully encrypted. Enter the export passphrase to import all of its contents.

ssh.authFailed: Authentication failed: incorrect username, password, or key.
ssh.keyEncrypted: The private key is encrypted. Enter the key passphrase in the connection settings.
ssh.keyUnsupportedFormat: Unsupported private key format: use OpenSSH format or legacy PEM (BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY). PKCS#8 (BEGIN PRIVATE KEY) can be converted with ssh-keygen -p -f <private-key> -m RFC4716.
ssh.noMatchingAlgo: Algorithm negotiation failed (for older devices, enable "Legacy algorithms" in the connection settings): {{msg}}
ssh.connRefused: Connection refused: the port on the target host is not open.

ssh.dnsResolveFail: Unable to resolve the host name.
ssh.handshakeLost: The connection dropped before the handshake: if this connection uses a proxy, first make sure the proxy is online; otherwise this is usually server-side rate limiting (sshd MaxStartups / fail2ban) or a network interruption.
ssh.proxyNotFound: The proxy referenced by this connection no longer exists. Re-select it under "Settings → Proxies & Keys", or switch the connection to direct.
ssh.proxyNoHost: Proxy "{{name}}" has no address. Fill it in under "Settings → Proxies & Keys".
ssh.noPrivateKeySelected: No private key selected. Choose a saved key in the connection settings.
ssh.privateKeyNotFound: The private key referenced by this connection no longer exists. Re-select it under "Settings → Proxies & Keys".
ssh.privateKeyReadFail: Cannot read the file for private key "{{name}}": {{path}}
ssh.noAgent: No SSH agent detected (start the ssh-agent service or set SSH_AUTH_SOCK).
ssh.nulByteInArg: The argument contains a NUL byte and cannot be passed as a shell argument.
ssh.transferClientNotReady: The transfer connection is not ready.
ssh.forwardInRejected: The remote host refused to listen on {{addr}}:{{port}} (addresses other than 127.0.0.1 require GatewayPorts enabled on the server).
ssh.openMonitorChannelFail: Failed to open the monitoring channel: {{reason}}
ssh.openTransferChannelFail: Failed to open the transfer channel: {{reason}}
ssh.profileNotFound: The connection profile does not exist.
ssh.sessionNotFound: The session does not exist or has been closed.
